scope: Refresh open-source DWG/DXF peer evidence and audit local drawing-date/time header conversion for an uncovered boundedness risk; update the implementation plan without changing code or support claims.

method.kind: Primary documentation, current public peer status, and local worktree source/test inspection
localInspection: src/intern/dxfreader.cpp: dxfReaderAscii::readDouble accepts finite values without domain-specific date/time bounds
src/drw_header.cpp: readJulianDate and splitTimeVar convert four HEADER variables between doubles and signed 32-bit day/millisecond pairs
src/intern/dwgwriter15.cpp and src/intern/dwgwriter18.cpp: duplicated splitAuxDate helpers encode TDCREATE/TDUPDATE in auxiliary headers
tests: no direct generated boundary coverage found for these four date/time variables or the duplicate auxiliary-header conversion

evidence.observed: The local user-provided ODA v5.4.1 PDF copy was found under the suffix (1). Its extracted pages 75–76 identify TDCREATE/TDUPDATE as Julian-day plus milliseconds-into-day pairs, and TDINDWG/TDUSRTIMER as days plus milliseconds-into-day pairs. The ODA reference remains the authority for exact DWG layout and version behavior.
doesNotEstablish: all legal numeric ranges, negative-value policy, or every version-specific precision rule
that local worktree conversion matches all producer profiles

evidence.observed: Autodesk documents TDCREATE/TDUPDATE as wall-clock date values and TDINDWG/TDUSRTIMER as elapsed time values, each represented by day plus fractional day in DXF; separate system-variable documentation notes second-only precision in AutoCAD 2017+ versus millisecond precision in earlier releases.
doesNotEstablish: DWG binary encoding or producer-specific rounding for all target versions
permission to normalize, truncate, or rewrite caller-supplied timestamps

evidence.observed: Open PR #1369 reports inconsistent TIMEBLL/TIMERLL-to-real projections across LibreDWG code paths and proposes correcting the Julian-day fraction. The PR states its binary writer uses the day/millisecond pair rather than the derived double; it remains peer work, not an executed current-release comparison.
doesNotEstablish: that the PR is merged or released

evidence.observed: The ASCII DXF numeric reader rejects non-finite doubles, but it accepts finite values without timestamp-specific day bounds. The local split helpers call floor/round and cast the integral day to int32 without an explicit range check; the code has separate duplicate helpers for the primary HEADER and AC1015+/modern auxiliary headers. No direct test coverage for this conversion was found.
doesNotEstablish: a reproduced crash, sanitizer finding, or native-file failure
the exact legal range until the matching ODA section is read

evidence.observed: GDAL documents binary DXF reading from 3.12, but its OGR projection tessellates many curves, excludes some OCS/elevation cases, and exposes modern ASM as raw data rather than solid geometry. ACadSharp v3.8.0 is a signed release, while its newest issue reports post-release behavior; open-source peers remain operation/version/feature scoped. These peer facts reinforce existing evidence lanes and add no new support result.
doesNotEstablish: full DXF semantic round-trip coverage from GDAL
independent ACIS/B-rep semantics from raw ASM exposure
that an open issue describes current released behavior

planImpact.orderReason: Prioritize a small header-value input-safety check before the next broader UCS writer slice; finish the relevant ODA v5.4.1 variable/version context review, then implement only checked conversion and focused tests.

version × operation × feature × consumer comparator matrix
